source_text: Si uetera fidei exempla, et Dei gratiam testificantia et aedificationem hominis operantia, propterea in litteris sunt digesta, ut lectione eorum quasi repraesentatione rerum et deus honoretur et homo confortetur: cur non et noua documenta aeque utrique causae conuenientia et digerantur? Uel quia proinde et haec uetera futura quandoque sunt et necessaria posteris, si in praesenti suo tempore minori deputantur auctoritati, propter praesumptam uenerationem antiquitatis. Sed uiderint qui unam uirtutem spiritus unius sancti pro aetatibus iudicent temporum: cum maiora reputanda sunt nouitiora quaeque ut nouissimiora, secundum exuperationem gratiae in ultima saeculi spatia decretam. In nouissimis enim diebus, dicit dominus, effundam de spiritu meo super omnem carnem, et prophetabunt filii filiaeque eorum; et super seruos et ancillas meas de meo spiritu effundam: et iuuenes uisiones uidebunt, et senes somnia somniabunt. Itaque et nos, qui sicut prophetias ita et uisiones nouas pariter repromissas et agnoscimus et honoramus, ceterasque uirtutes spiritus sancti ad instrumentum ecclesiae deputatas (cui et missus est idem omnia donatiua administrans in omnibus prout uni cuique distribuit dominus) necessario et digerimus et ad gloriam dei lectione celebramus, ut ne qua aut imbecillitas aut desperatio fidei apud ueteres tantum aestimet gratiam diuinitus conuersatam, siue in martyrum siue in reuelationum dignatione: cum semper deus operetur quae repromisit, non credentibus in testimonium, credentibus in beneficium. Sed nos itaque quod audiuimus et contrectauimus annuntiamus et uobis, fratres et filioli: ut et uos qui interfuistis rememoremini gloriae domini, et qui nunc cognoscitis per auditum communionem habeatis cum sanctis martyribus, et per illos cum domino Iesu Christo: cui est claritas et honor in saecula saeculorum, amen.
thought_title: Why new martyrdoms must be written down
orientation: The anonymous editor opens the work by arguing that recent visions and martyrdoms have the same authority as ancient ones.
pass_a_gloss: If ancient examples of faith, both bearing witness to the grace of God and working the building up of man, for this reason have been set in order in writings, so that by the reading of them as if by a making present of the things both God may be honored and man may be strengthened: why should not also new evidences equally fitting to each cause also be set in order? Or because these new things also will at some time be ancient and necessary for posterity, if in their own present time they are assigned to lesser authority, on account of presumed veneration of antiquity. But let them see to it who judge the one power of the one Holy Spirit according to ages of times: when the newer things, as the most recent things, ought to be reckoned greater, according to the abundance of grace decreed for the last stretches of the age. For in the last days, says the Lord, I will pour out from my Spirit upon all flesh, and their sons and their daughters will prophesy; and upon my servants and my maidservants I will pour out from my Spirit: and young men will see visions, and old men will dream dreams. Therefore also we, who both recognize and honor alike prophecies and new visions as equally promised again, and the other powers of the Holy Spirit assigned for the equipment of the church (to which also the same Spirit was sent administering all gifts in all as the Lord distributed to each one) necessarily both set them in order and celebrate them by reading to the glory of God, in order that no weakness or despair of faith may judge the grace of God to have dwelt only among the ancients, whether in the favor shown to martyrs or to revelations: since God always works what he promised again, for those not believing for testimony, for those believing for benefit. But we therefore announce also to you, brothers and little children, what we heard and touched, so that both you who were present may remember the glory of the Lord, and you who now know through hearing may have fellowship with the holy martyrs, and through them with the Lord Jesus Christ: to whom is brightness and honor into ages of ages, amen.

pass_b_english: Ancient examples of faith were set in order in writing because they bear witness to God's grace and build people up. When they are read, the events are made present again, so God is honored and people are strengthened. Why should new evidences not also be set in order when they serve those same two purposes? These new accounts will one day be ancient themselves and necessary for posterity, even if in their own time they are granted less authority because people assume that antiquity deserves reverence. Let those answer for it who judge the one power of the one Holy Spirit by the ages of time, since each newer work, as the latest, should be counted greater, in keeping with the abundance of grace decreed for the final stretches of the age.

For the Lord says in Scripture, "In the last days I will pour out my Spirit on all people, and your sons and daughters will prophesy; I will pour out my Spirit on my servants, both men and women, and your young men will see visions, and your old men will dream dreams" (Joel 2:28-29; Acts 2:17-18; the Latin follows the author's wording). So we recognize and honor prophecies and new visions alike as promised, together with the other powers of the Holy Spirit assigned as equipment for the church. He was sent to the church, administering all his gifts among all people as the Lord assigns to each one. Of necessity we set these accounts in order and celebrate them by reading to God's glory.

We do this so no weakness or despair in faith will suppose that divine grace dwelt only among the ancients, whether shown in the honor given to martyrs or in revelations. For God always does what he promised, for unbelievers for testimony and for believers for benefit. So what we heard and touched we announce also to you, brothers and little children (1 John 1:1-3). Then you who were present will remember the glory of the Lord, and you who now learn by hearing will have fellowship with the holy martyrs, and through them with the Lord Jesus Christ, to whom are glory and honor forever and ever, amen.
